body: claimed: mkinney (Claude agent) · 2026-11-08T20:57Z · branch issue/44-incremental-ring-walk · plan: make the growth-ring walk re-walk only the changed stretch of the outline per revolution (same rings, bit-for-bit where possible), split adaptive/mod.rs under 400 lines, and lift the #13 budget so a long band keeps its spiral - pinned by an app/motion test on a long channel.

Claim withdrawn (mkinney, Claude agent). What was learned, measured with the #13 budgets lifted (release, `adaptive_band`, band round the 60 x 50 part); no code landed:

- **14 mm band:** plans in 23.7 s (work 54,178 tool radii vs today's 30,000 cap; 2,469 trial revolutions on ~885-vertex rings) but **overloads every revolution from rev 52** at margin 2.4 - worst 91.5 % of D at (63.76, 54.15) vs the 14.6 % optimum, engagement 133-144 deg vs the 47.5 deg bound ("no step held the load"). Margins 1.0 and 1.6 run out of margin first.
- **20 mm band:** plans in 19.3 s but overloads from rev ~7 (58-85 deg) and is then refused by the travel budget (`pocket_hsm::over_budget`: 9,980 mm out of cut for 5,372 mm in cut).
- **Where the time goes:** polygon geometry (offset / intersect / opening of the whole ring, plus the margin offset every revolution) ~87 %; the stock-bitmap walk ~11 %. An incremental *walk* alone trims ~11 %.

Why an incremental walk can't deliver the issue's goal:
1. The wall margin closes by `GAP` (2.5 um) every revolution to keep rings strictly nested, capping a spiral at ~140 (margin 1.0) to ~236 (1.6) revolutions; a 4 mm channel whose fronts hold the load at 0.12-0.37 mm/rev needs ~400-1,100. Speed doesn't change that count.
2. The load law fails in channels - the same open problem as #7 round 8.
3. The travel rule refuses long bands regardless: one spiral flies ~one cleared length per revolution while cutting only the two fronts.
4. Making the geometry local (windows round the fronts, stitched to the walls) changes vertices, so goldens move; and the moving margin means no wall stretch is strictly unchanged.

A real fix is a channel-growth redesign: freeze stretches that reached the wall and advance only the fronts (breaks the "each revolution encloses all before" no-crossing proof, so it needs a new one), a front step law that holds the load in a channel narrower than the tool, and a travel rule that doesn't charge lifted returns against the spiral. The 400-line split of `adaptive/mod.rs` (now 435 lines) is still owed; it's best done with that redesign.
Claim recorded for @mkinney - label and assignee set (only collaborators can set labels; your comment is the claim).

Releasing this: the claim from 2026-11-08 has no branch or PR behind it, and it shouldn't block other contributors. The issue is free to pick up.

claimed: issue-worker-high (Opus 5.5) · 2026-11-11T14:45Z · worktree/branch .claude/worktrees/issue-44 / issue/44-incremental-ring-walk · plan: incremental walk = per revolution, walk only the stretch of the morph that leaves the previous revolution's swept band (samples farther than h/2 from the last ring, found by a distance test against the previous ring; the stock outside it is reused as-is), cache invalidated when the margin steps, the fillet level changes or a trial aborts; first measure on the island fixture (`HSM_ONE=island hsm_one`, instrumented, local only) what share of trial-walk length is "live" (removes cells or reads contact) vs the summed revolution length the #13 counter charges, and the walk's share of wall time - that ceiling decides whether it is a PR or a stop. Band readings taken from the 2026-11-08 comment, not repeated.

Stopped - no PR. The incremental walk does not hold; measured, not argued. issue-worker-high (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-11.

**Scheme tried:** per revolution, walk only the stretch of the morph that leaves the previous revolution's swept band; reuse the stock elsewhere; invalidate on a margin step, a fillet-level change or an aborted trial. That only pays if most of each revolution is "dead" (reads no stock, removes no cell).

**Readings** (release, instrumented probe, tree = origin/main 4865500d + #848's fix merged locally only; probe on branch `issue/44-incremental-ring-walk`, commit 1dc7b945, DO NOT MERGE - `PROBE_LIFT=1` lifts the #13 budgets):

| fixture | grow() call | work (r, cumulative) | grow time | stock-walk time | samples that read stock or cut | samples that remove a cell | samples biting >15 deg |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| island 60x40, 12x12 (budgets as on main) | margin 1.0 -> Short | 13,737 | 34.2 s | 4.9 s | 97.5 % | 38.6 % | 52.9 % |
| | margin 1.6 -> **Refused** (163 revs) | 30,222 | 34.0 s | 5.8 s | 99.3 % | 35.7 % | 50.6 % |
| band 14 mm (budgets lifted) | margin 1.0 -> Short | 8,307 | 14.7 s | 3.3 s | 98.1 % | 50.4 % | 59.9 % |
| | margin 1.6 -> Short | 27,589 | 24.2 s | 6.8 s | 98.6 % | 41.0 % | 51.1 % |
| | margin 2.4 -> Done | 54,178 | 14.8 s | 3.5 s | 99.5 % | 29.2 % | 41.2 % |

The band's 54,178 r and its 91.5 % D overload reproduce the 2026-11-08 comment exactly (the probe changes nothing).

**Why it does not hold:**
1. **No local stretch to reuse.** 97.5-99.5 % of every trial walk reads stock and 30-50 % of it removes cells. The wall margin closes by `GAP` every revolution, so the wall runs shave the margin strip all round the ring each time - the change is global, not a front-local stretch. Skipping the "dead" part saves at most ~2 % of the walk.
2. **The walk is not where the time goes.** The stock walk is 15 % (island) to 25 % (band) of grow time. The rest is whole-ring polygon work: offset of the cleared region, intersect with the margin area, opening, all per trial. Even a free walk leaves the island at ~58 s and the band at ~40 s.
3. **The quadratic is in the toolpath, not the planner.** The #13 counter sums revolution lengths, and one spiral's own emitted length is that sum. In a channel it is quadratic in channel length by construction: every revolution encloses everything before it. The band plan rides 13,322 mm of wall to clear ~1.1 m of channel and is overloaded anyway. A faster planner does not change that.
4. **Byte-identical is impossible:** a skipped stretch drops readings that feed the worst angle the step search keeps, so the path would move.

**New fact for #845 and #13:** on main today the island fixture spends **~68 s (release)** in two grow() calls before the 30,000 r budget refuses it. It runs at about 2.2 ms per tool radius of work, against about 1 ms/r on the band. The budget in tool radii does not bound wall time: #13's "plans in seconds or refuses" does not hold on the island. #845's held fix roughly doubles that work, and an incremental walk would not pay for it (point 2).

**Recommendation for the maintainer:**
- **(a)** Accept the named Offset-ring fallback for long channels and bands as the behaviour, and close #44 as won't-do. The spiral's own path length is the obstacle, not planner speed.
- **(b)** Separately, file a P1 issue to bound grow() by time as well as by work, for example an up-front estimate that also refuses the island class sooner. Today it costs ~68 s before falling back.
- **(c)** If a spiral in channels is still wanted, it is the channel-growth redesign the 2026-11-08 comment describes: freeze the stretches that reached the wall and advance only the fronts, with a new no-crossing proof, a front step law for channels and a travel rule for lifted returns. That is `effort:max`, research-shaped work.

The `adaptive/mod.rs` split (435 lines) is still owed. It is a behaviour-neutral refactor and could be its own `effort:medium` issue; it was not done here because there is no PR.

Claim released. The tier was not the limit: the scheme itself fails on the numbers.

Won't do (maintainer, 2026-11-11): long channels and thin bands keep the named Offset-ring fallback. The measurements above show an incremental walk cannot help: 97.5-99.5 % of every revolution's walk touches stock, the walk is only 15-25 % of planner time, and the work grows with the square of the channel length because every revolution encloses everything before it. A spiral in channels would need a channel-growth redesign (new algorithm); open a research item if that is ever wanted. The file split this issue also asked for is #851; the planner's time bound is #850 / PR #865. The diagnostic probe stays on branch issue/44-incremental-ring-walk (do not merge).
